label: Heavy social-media user with elevated loneliness, depression, and anxiety symptoms
summary: This profile is characterized by comparatively high loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms alongside heavy daily social-media use. In the training split, respondents in this group averaged just over five hours of social-media use per day.
demographic_anchor: Female respondent, graduate education or above, and more than 5 hours of daily social-media use.
behavior_markers: Reports heavier daily social-media use
Shows higher average loneliness scores
Shows higher average depressive symptom scores
Shows higher average anxiety symptom scores
tone: Vulnerable, digitally immersed, and emotionally strained

label: Low-distress heavy social-media user
summary: Respondents in this profile report relatively low loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms, while also showing comparatively high daily social-media use.
demographic_anchor: Typically represented by a female respondent with graduate-level education or above and about 3-5 hours of daily social-media use.
behavior_markers: Uses social media heavily on a daily basis, with an average near 4.7 hours per day.
Reports low average loneliness (UCLA-8 mean approximately 1.13).
Reports low average depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 mean approximately 0.73).
Reports low average anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean approximately 0.61).
tone: Connected, emotionally stable, and digitally engaged.

label: Low-distress light social-media user
summary: This profile is characterized by comparatively low loneliness, low depressive symptoms, and low anxiety symptoms, alongside light daily social-media use.
demographic_anchor: More commonly represented by men with graduate-level education or higher who report using social media for less than 1 hour per day.
behavior_markers: Uses social media lightly, with a daily midpoint around 0.5 hours
Reports low average loneliness (UCLA-8 mean 1.25)
Reports low average depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 mean 0.90)
Reports low average anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean 0.89)
tone: Stable, low-distress, and lightly engaged online

label: High distress, heavy social-media use
summary: Respondents in this profile report comparatively higher loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms, alongside the heaviest daily social-media use among the summarized groups.
demographic_anchor: Female respondents with graduate-level education or above who report more than 5 hours of daily social-media use.
behavior_markers: Reports higher loneliness on the UCLA-8 indicator
Shows elevated depressive symptoms on the PHQ-9 indicator
Shows elevated anxiety symptoms on the GAD-7 indicator
Uses social media heavily on a daily basis, with an average above 5 hours per day
tone: Vulnerable, digitally immersed, and emotionally strained

label: Lower loneliness, elevated anxiety and depressive symptoms, lighter social-media use
summary: This profile reflects respondents with comparatively low loneliness alongside higher anxiety symptoms and somewhat elevated depressive symptoms, while reporting lighter daily social-media use than heavier-use groups.
demographic_anchor: Male respondents, typically educated to graduate level or above, with about 3–5 hours of daily social-media use.
behavior_markers: Reports relatively low loneliness on the UCLA-8 measure.
Shows elevated anxiety symptoms, with anxiety appearing more pronounced than depression.
Shows higher depressive symptoms compared with lower-symptom groups.
Uses social media for a moderate-to-lighter amount of time, with an average around 2.6 hours per day.
Combines internalizing symptoms with lower perceived social disconnection.
tone: Concerned but socially connected; emotionally strained without strong signs of loneliness.

label: Low Distress, Light Social-Media Use
summary: Respondents in this profile show comparatively low loneliness, low depressive symptoms, and low anxiety symptoms, alongside lighter daily social-media use.
demographic_anchor: Typically represented by a female respondent with graduate-level education or above and about 1–3 hours of daily social-media use.
behavior_markers: Reports low average loneliness (UCLA-8 mean: 1.19)
Reports low average depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 mean: 0.83)
Reports low average anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean: 0.90)
Uses social media lightly, averaging about 2 hours per day
tone: Stable, low-distress, and moderate in daily digital engagement.
